judged_text: Attendee rows are committed via prisma.booking.update/createMany before the external eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call, with no transaction or rollback joining the two. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (calendar API auth/network failure), the mutation rejects with an error toast while the guests are already persisted; every retry then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 branch and fails with BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', leaving the organizer unable to complete an operation that half-succeeded, with no notification emails ever sent.

record.issue_text: [BUG] Attendee rows are committed via prisma.booking.update/createMany before the external eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call, with no transaction or rollback joining the two. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (calendar API auth/network failure), the mutation rejects with an error toast while the guests are already persisted; every retry then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 branch and fails with BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', leaving the organizer unable to complete an operation that half-succeeded, with no notification emails ever sent.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists new attendees first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no transaction/rollback linking the DB write and the external calendar update. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the RPC will reject (no surrounding try/catch), the UI will show an error toast (`onError` in `AddGuestsDialog`), but the guests are already stored. A retry with the same emails will compute `uniqueGuests` by filtering out existing attendees and can hit `uniqueGuests.length === 0` leading to `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), and the email notification block is after the calendar update so it won’t run in that failure path.
